messages:
Ana: quick heads-up — during the IR tabletop this morning the onprem keystore-agent (v1.3.2) accepted a decrypt call from a service account that appears to be scoped to multiple tenants. we reproduced it in the lab; not seen in prod logs so far but we should treat as a vuln. need three things: RBAC tightening, audit-log enrichment, and network-policy egress restrictions. @ops-liz can you own coordinating the follow-ups? :warning:

Tom: can you paste the minimal repro info and the agent logs we captured?

Ana: repro steps below, super short:
1) run agent w/ test svcacc token that has both tenant-a and tenant-b decrypt privileges
2) call /v1/decrypt with tenant-b ciphertext but headers for tenant-a
3) agent returns plaintext (unexpected)

Ana: log excerpt:
```
2025-09-12T14:03:21Z keystore-agent[pid=421] INFO request="decrypt" svcacc=svc-teamx tenant_requested=tenant-b tenant_context=tenant-a request_id=abcd-1234 outcome=allowed
```

Jess: ugh. ok first: RBAC change — make decrypt authorization check evaluate the tenant_ctx derived from the ciphertext envelope and the caller svcacc scopes; fail closed on mismatch. second: we need audit logs to include both tenant_requested and envelope_tenant and a correlated request_id so SIEM can stitch events. third: network policy — keystore-agent should only be allowed to talk to our local KMS endpoint and the internal metadata service; drop wide egress rules.

Kevin: agree. two implementation notes: 1) adding envelope_tenant to logs is cheap, but we should avoid logging plaintext or full ciphertext. 2) RBAC check will need a migration path — we should deploy a dual-mode: warn-only first (log mismatch) for 48h then enforce.

Ana: suggested audit log shape (minimal):
```
{
  "ts":"2025-09-12T14:03:21Z",
  "svc":"keystore-agent",
  "request_id":"abcd-1234",
  "caller":"svc-teamx",
  "caller_scopes":["decrypt:tenant-a"],
  "envelope_tenant":"tenant-b",
  "action":"decrypt",
  "outcome":"warn_mismatch"
}
```

Jess: nice. also add a field ksm_request_id that we propagate from agent -> kms so we can correlate KMS audit entries with agent-side entries. we should push that to SIEM as structured JSON.

Tom: ops question — what about performance / latency if we add extra KMS metadata propagation? will be small but call path increases. Kevin?

Kevin: minimal perf diff. biggest cost is any extra KMS calls. prefer to pass an existing correlation header (X-Request-ID) instead of additional roundtrips. agent already sends a single decrypt RPC; attach header and log it.

ops-liz: @Ana I'll take coordination. I'll open a single ticket in our tracker and an on-call pager duty runbook update PR. can you assign owners for: RBAC change, audit enrichment, network policy, runbook update?

Ana: assigning now: RBAC owner = Tom, audit/enrichment = Jess, netpol = Kevin, runbook + postmortem doc = ops-liz. i'll add repro and the log excerpts to the ticket.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20250912-0073 | Keystore agent cross-tenant decrypt (tabletop) — severity: advisory | Owner: ops-liz

Jess: vuln triage notes: mark as P2 (no evidence of exploit), plan: 1) instrument warn-only in 24h 2) collect 48h of logs, 3) enforce deny after review, 4) run a canary on staging and dedicated clusters. also update alerting to fire on any decrypt outcome==allowed where envelope_tenant != caller_tenant.

Tom: putting together a small k8s NetworkPolicy snippet as starting point — allow agent -> kms + metadata only:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-egress-lockdown
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: internal-kms
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: infra-services
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

Kevin: nice. also ensure our egress proxy (sidecar) enforces mTLS to KMS and strips any upstream public egress.

ops-liz: i'll file the tracker ticket now and add the checklist. target: warn-only rollout in 24-36h, collect logs for 48h, then enforcement the following week. any objections?

Jess: no objections. please add test prompts for canary verifying allowed vs denied behavior.

Ana: thanks all. i'll follow up in the ticket with repro artifacts and a short tabletop write-up for the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
